description: 2 tactical challenges for Black in the Najdorf Poisoned Pawn. Grab the b2 pawn with 7...Qb6 and navigate the complications a pawn up.

drills.briefExplanation: 7...Qb6 Qd2 8...Qxb2 9.Rb1 Qa3 — take the pawn, then run the queen to safety and consolidate.
drills.description: Black to play. White's 7.f4 signals aggression — answer with the Poisoned Pawn grab 7...Qb6.
drills.explanation: 7...Qb6 is Black's most principled reply to 7.f4, immediately questioning b2. After 8.Qd2 Qxb2 Black is a pawn up; the queen's escape 9...Qa3 is the critical retreat, keeping an eye on b2 while dodging Rb1 tempo. Then 10...Nc6 develops and prepares ...e5 or ...Be7 — Black's extra pawn is real if the king survives the coming f5 break.
drills.name: Grabbing the Pawn

drills.briefExplanation: 8...Qxb2 9.Rb1 Qa3 10.f5 Nc6 11.fxe6 fxe6 — accept the pawn, return it at the right moment, and trade into an endgame a pawn up.
drills.description: Black to play. The queen stands on b6 and White has committed to 8.Qd2 — take the pawn and find the consolidation.
drills.explanation: After 8...Qxb2 9.Rb1 Qa3 White's 10.f5 is the critical test. Black meets it head-on: 10...Nc6 11.fxe6 fxe6 opens the f-file but also the e-file for Black's rooks. The point is that after the coming exchanges Black's extra pawn and bishop pair give lasting chances — the poison only kills if Black panics.
drills.name: Consolidating a Pawn Up
